answers.text: Tell the assistant every drop-off message should come back as three lines, always the same order: drop-off time, then pallet count, then any damage noted, one fact per line.
List every call from the week with time, customer, topic and outcome, and count how many say 'follow-up needed' in the outcome column for the total at the top.
The finishing time doesn't work — access starts at 8am on the 22nd and the crew only needs about six hours, so they'd be done early afternoon that same day, not on the 23rd like the note says.
The 20% increase doesn't check out — 96 up to 118 is closer to a 23% rise, not 20%.

I'd sign off the second one, it gives the actual ticket counts, 940 total and 827 within SLA, so you can see exactly where the 88% comes from. The first one just states the percentage — looks fine, but there's no way to check it without running the numbers again yourself.

I'd send the second one, the volume numbers back up the ask for a better rate. The first one might be fine too, it's just that 'we'd expect a better rate' doesn't say based on what, so there's nothing there yet to point to if they ask.

1. Careful with the line pricing. 2. Yes, that's fine, it's just a total. 3. No, that budget's not signed off. 4. Better not, hasn't been checked. 5. No, that's someone's home address, definitely not.

The hourly rates and the retainer cap I'd leave out, and the non-disclosure clause too since it names the client directly. The general service scope is fine to paste, there's nothing sensitive in what work is covered.
Before the stock-reconciliation summary goes out each month, I'd check the counted total against the warehouse system record.

I'd put the gate on the last step, before the payment note gets submitted automatically — once that's gone through it's hard to pull back. I'd also keep an eye on the first step, since if the invoice gets misread the check downstream is only as good as that. The gate should check that the matched amount is actually within the stated tolerance, not just that a match was found.
